newsitem.title: USA: US utilities ask for escrow of nuclear waste funds.
newsitem.headline: US utilities ask for escrow of nuclear waste funds.

text.p: Utilities and states that are suing the U.S. Energy Department over nuclear waste disposal Wednesday asked a federal court to order the department to have a plan within 30 days on how it will start removing waste from power plants.
The parties also asked the federal court for permission to immediately escrow $600 million in annual payments to the U.S. Nuclear Waste Fund until the department "meets its legal obligations."

The U.S. Court of Appeals last July said the Energy Department is legally obligated to take control of the radioactive waste starting January 31, 1998, a deadline the Energy Department has said it cannot meet.
The department is evaluating whether to put a permanent waste repository in Yucca Mountain in Nevada, but that facility would not be ready for about another 15 years.

"We want DOE to perform its nuclear waste disposal obligations. Americans have paid over $13 billion for nulcear waste disposal under contracts DOE says it will not perform," Kris Sanda, Minnesota Public Service Commissioner, said in a statement.
